message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"8.21","text":"For the temporary king once approached the king of our piety, not using force (for that was not permitted), but exhorting and persuading, because being persuaded lies within each person’s own power. So he approached as king of present things and said to the king of things to come, “All the kingdoms of the present world are subject to me; moreover, the gold and the silver and all the luxury of this world are under my authority. Therefore, fall down and worship me, and I will give you all these things.” He said this knowing that, with that act of worship, he would also gain authority over him, and so the latter would deprive himself of the glory and kingdom to come. Knowing these things, the latter not only did not worship him, but did not even wish to receive anything that he offered. For he would thereby have pledged himself as security together with his own possessions—that is, from then on he would no longer be permitted even to touch any of the things returned to him. He therefore answered, “It is written: ‘You shall fear the Lord your God and serve him alone.’”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῷ γὰρ τῆς εὐσεβείας ἡμῶν βασιλεῖ","chosen":"the king of our piety","rationale":"Preserves the unusual genitive description rather than replacing it with a familiar Christological title."},{"source_quote":"ὁ πρόσκαιρος βασιλεύς","chosen":"the temporary king","rationale":"πρόσκαιρος marks limited duration and contrasts this ruler with the king of things to come."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ τοῦ προσκυνῆσαι καὶ τὴν κατ’ αὐτοῦ εἶχεν ἐξουσίαν","chosen":"with that act of worship, he would also gain authority over him","rationale":"Takes the temporary king as the one gaining authority and the future king as the one placed under it; κατ’ αὐτοῦ can express authority directed against or over someone."},{"source_quote":"καὶ οὕτως τῆς μελλούσης δόξης καὶ βασιλείας ἑαυτὸν ἀφῄρει","chosen":"and so the latter would deprive himself of the glory and kingdom to come","rationale":"Supplies the future king as the subject of ἀφῄρει because worship would threaten his future glory and kingdom, although the Greek does not explicitly mark the change of subject from the temporary king."},{"source_quote":"ἑαυτὸν γὰρ σὺν τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ κατενεχύραζεν","chosen":"For he would thereby have pledged himself as security together with his own possessions","rationale":"Renders the security or pledge imagery of κατενεχύραζεν and treats the imperfect as the consequence that accepting the offer would have entailed."},{"source_quote":"φοβηθήσῃ","chosen":"You shall fear","rationale":"Follows the supplied Greek rather than harmonizing the quotation with a familiar temptation narrative using “worship.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ταῦτα δὲ ἔλεγεν εἰδὼς ὅτι μετὰ τοῦ προσκυνῆσαι καὶ τὴν κατ’ αὐτοῦ εἶχεν ἐξουσίαν καὶ οὕτως τῆς μελλούσης δόξης καὶ βασιλείας ἑαυτὸν ἀφῄρει","issue":"The unexpressed subject of ἀφῄρει is materially ambiguous. The main text takes it to be the future king, who would deprive himself of the coming glory and kingdom by worshiping; alternatively, the subject may continue to be the temporary king from εἶχεν, despite the resulting contextual difficulty. This is a provisional contextual interpretation, not a correction of the supplied text.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἑαυτὸν γὰρ σὺν τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ κατενεχύραζεν, ὅπερ ἐστὶν μὴ ἐξεῖναι τοῦ λοιποῦ τῶν αὐτῷ ἀποδοθέντων μηδὲ ψαῦσαι ἔτι","issue":"The subject of κατενεχύραζεν and the referent of αὐτῷ are not explicit. The translation continues the future king as the implied subject and takes αὐτῷ as referring to him; alternatively, one or both may refer to the temporary king. The supplied construction is translatable without emendation.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"8.22","text":"Nevertheless, after the king of the impious had tried in many ways to draw the king of the devout toward his own will and was unable, he ceased his effort to ensnare him in the remaining areas of his way of life. But you, because you were ignorant of the law laid down beforehand, came under his authority through evil deeds. Therefore, you were defiled in body and soul, and in the present you are abused by both sufferings and demons, while in what is to come you will have souls destined to be punished. You are not the only ones who have suffered this through ignorance, but so have some from our own nation. Having been seized beforehand for evil deeds by the ruler of wickedness, they were then invited as though to a banquet by a father celebrating a wedding for his son, but they did not obey. In place of those who disobeyed because of that prior seizure, the father celebrating the wedding for his son commanded us through the prophet of truth, when we had gone to the outlets of the roads (that is, toward you), to put a clean wedding garment around you (which is baptism, performed for forgiveness of the evil deeds you have committed) and to bring into God’s banquet those who have become good through a change of heart, even if they had at first been left out of the feast.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὰ λοιπὰ τῆς πολιτείας","chosen":"in the remaining areas of his way of life","rationale":"πολιτεία here denotes conduct or manner of life, not a political constitution."},{"source_quote":"τὸν προορισθέντα νόμον","chosen":"the law laid down beforehand","rationale":"Preserves the prior determination expressed by προορισθέντα without importing a later doctrinal sense of predestination."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τοῦ τῆς κακίας ἡγεμόνος προληφθέντες","chosen":"having been seized beforehand by the ruler of wickedness","rationale":"The passive verb depicts prior capture or preemption and prepares for the related noun πρόληψιν."},{"source_quote":"καθαρὸν ἔνδυμα γάμου περιβαλεῖν","chosen":"to put a clean wedding garment around you","rationale":"The person being clothed is implicit; the parenthetical identification with baptism for the audience’s past deeds supports taking the audience as the recipient."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τοὺς ἀγαθοὺς εἰς τὸ θεοῦ δεῖπνον εἰσάγειν ἐκ τῆς μεταμελείας","chosen":"and to bring into God’s banquet those who have become good through a change of heart","rationale":"The main text relates ἐκ τῆς μεταμελείας to τοὺς ἀγαθούς, understanding the people as good through moral reconsideration. μεταμέλεια may denote change of heart, regret, or reconsideration. The phrase may instead modify εἰσάγειν, yielding “to bring the good into God’s banquet on account of their change of heart.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἐπαύσατο, πρὸς τὰ λοιπὰ τῆς πολιτείας θηρεύειν αὐτὸν ἐπιχειρῶν","issue":"The present participle ἐπιχειρῶν may describe the effort that ceased or an attendant attempt made before or while he ceased. The translation takes the attempt to ensnare him as the effort that ceased; the alternative attachment does not require a textual correction.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καθαρὸν ἔνδυμα γάμου περιβαλεῖν","issue":"The person around whom the garment is to be placed is not expressed. The translation supplies “you” from the immediately preceding parenthesis and the following reference to deeds committed by the audience; “those encountered at the roads” is a broader possible referent.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καὶ τοὺς ἀγαθοὺς εἰς τὸ θεοῦ δεῖπνον εἰσάγειν ἐκ τῆς μεταμελείας","issue":"The attachment of ἐκ τῆς μεταμελείας is not explicit. The main text takes it with τοὺς ἀγαθούς, describing people who have become good through a change of heart. Alternatively, it may modify εἰσάγειν, so that their change of heart or regret provides the grounds for bringing the good into God’s banquet. Both readings are possible without altering the supplied Greek.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"8.23","text":"Therefore, if you wish to become a garment of the divine spirit, first make every effort to strip off the filthy hold already laid on you (which is an unclean spirit) and the defiled covering. You cannot strip this off in any other way unless you are first baptized on the basis of good deeds and then, having become clean in both body and soul, enjoy the eternal kingdom that is to come. Therefore, do not put your trust in idols or share a defiled table with them. Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not hate those whom it is not right to hate, do not steal, and do not set yourselves to any evil deeds at all. Otherwise, deprived of the hope of the good things to come, in the present you will be beset by both evil demons and painful afflictions, while in the coming age you will be punished with eternal fire. What has been said to you today is sufficient. Now, those of you troubled by afflictions, remain for healing; among the others, those who wish may go in peace.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἔνδυμα οὖν εἰ βούλεσθε γενέσθαι θείου πνεύματος","chosen":"if you wish to become a garment of the divine spirit","rationale":"Preserves the source’s image of people becoming the spirit’s garment rather than merely being clothed by the spirit."},{"source_quote":"τὸ ῥυπαρὸν ὑμῶν πρόλημμα","chosen":"the filthy hold already laid on you","rationale":"In context πρόλημμα denotes a prior possession or seizure, identified immediately as an unclean spirit; “preconception” would obscure that contextual image."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ καλαῖς πράξεσιν βαπτισθῆτε","chosen":"you are baptized on the basis of good deeds","rationale":"Takes ἐπί with the dative as expressing a basis or condition. Other viable nuances are “in connection with good deeds” or “with a view to good deeds.”"},{"source_quote":"μὴ μισήσητε οὓς μὴ δίκαιον","chosen":"do not hate those whom it is not right to hate","rationale":"Retains the source’s qualification rather than broadening it into an unqualified prohibition of all hatred."},{"source_quote":"ὑπό τε κακῶν δαιμόνων καὶ χαλεπῶν παθημάτων συνελασθήσεσθε","chosen":"you will be beset by both evil demons and painful afflictions","rationale":"συνελαύνω depicts being driven together, hemmed in, or hard-pressed; “beset” conveys that force naturally."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ καλαῖς πράξεσιν βαπτισθῆτε","issue":"The force of ἐπί with the dative is contextually open: it may express basis or condition, association, or purpose. The main rendering selects basis, while “with a view to good deeds” remains viable. No alteration of the supplied text is required.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"8.24","text":"When he had said these things, everyone remained—some for the sake of being healed, and others in order to observe those who obtained healing. Peter merely laid his hands on them and prayed, and he healed them, so that those healed immediately became overjoyed, while those who had observed were extraordinarily amazed and, after praising God, believed with assured hope. Together with those who had been healed, they went away to their own homes under instructions to gather early the next day. After they had left, Peter remained there with his companions, partook of food, and gave himself rest in sleep.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἱστορῆσαι τοὺς τῆς θεραπείας ἐπιτυγχάνοντας","chosen":"in order to observe those who obtained healing","rationale":"ἱστορέω can mean inquire into or observe closely; remaining at the scene to witness healings supports “observe.”"},{"source_quote":"τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς ἐπιθεὶς μόνον καὶ εὐξάμενος ἰάσατο","chosen":"merely laid his hands on them and prayed, and he healed them","rationale":"μόνον emphasizes the simplicity of Peter’s actions as the means accompanying the healing."},{"source_quote":"βεβαίας ἐλπίδος πιστεύειν","chosen":"believed with assured hope","rationale":"Treats the genitive phrase as characterizing the hope accompanying their belief; “believed in a sure hope” is possible but less natural in context."},{"source_quote":"πρωΐτερον τῇ ὑστεραίᾳ","chosen":"early the next day","rationale":"πρωΐτερον functions adverbially of an early time on the following day."},{"source_quote":"διανέπαυσεν ἑαυτὸν τῷ ὕπνῳ","chosen":"gave himself rest in sleep","rationale":"Preserves the reflexive and the explicit reference to sleep rather than reducing the expression simply to “slept.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"βεβαίας ἐλπίδος πιστεύειν","issue":"The genitive βεβαίας ἐλπίδος has more than one defensible relation to πιστεύειν. The translation takes it as a genitive characterizing the manner or quality of belief; an alternative is “believed in a sure hope.” The construction remains intelligible without conjecture.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
